verdict.rationale: Unity's own docs say the Asset Database tracks source files and their imported counterparts to keep them in sync, and that the import process converts incoming assets automatically. The Editor can also be launched from the command line to automate workflows, and its public APIs allow deeper customization. However, nothing in the pack documents import hooks, import presets, or scripted per-asset processing, so only the baseline automatic import is evidenced. Missing for 10: documented import hooks (asset postprocessor callbacks), import presets, pipeline scripts that set import settings in bulk, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a technical artist, asset import is automatable — import hooks, presets, and pipeline scripts process incoming assets without hand-clicking each one

citations.quote: The asset import process converts most asset types from their original format to one optimized for use at authoring time and runtime.
The Asset Database stores information about the original source asset files and their imported counterparts to keep the two sets of data in sync.
You can launch the Unity Editor and Player with additional command line arguments to control startup behavior, configure settings, or automate workflows.
